intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that osteogenesis imperfecta type X (OI10) is caused by homozygous mutation in the SERPINH1 gene (600943) on chromosome 11q13.

checks.claim: Osteogenesis imperfecta type X (OI10) is caused by homozygous mutation in the SERPINH1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity for a missense mutation in SERPINH1, which encodes the collagen chaperone protein HSP47, results in severe recessive osteogenesis imperfecta.
checks.explanation: The title states that homozygosity for a SERPINH1 mutation causes recessive OI. The OI10 label is standard naming and does not appear in the abstract.

checks.claim: The SERPINH1 gene is located on chromosome 11q13.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified an autosomal-recessive missense mutation (c.233T>C, p.Leu78Pro) in SERPINH1
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention 11q13, but a gene's chromosomal location counts as standard nomenclature restating the gene.

paragraphs.text: Osteogenesis imperfecta type X is a severe autosomal recessive form of osteogenesis imperfecta caused by mutation in SERPINH1, which encodes the collagen chaperone-like protein HSP47 (Christiansen et al., 2010).

checks.claim: Osteogenesis imperfecta type X is a severe form of osteogenesis imperfecta.
checks.evidence_quote: results in severe recessive osteogenesis imperfecta
checks.explanation: The title calls the disorder severe.

checks.claim: Osteogenesis imperfecta type X is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified an autosomal-recessive missense mutation (c.233T>C, p.Leu78Pro) in SERPINH1
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the mutation as autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: Osteogenesis imperfecta type X is caused by mutation in SERPINH1.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified an autosomal-recessive missense mutation (c.233T>C, p.Leu78Pro) in SERPINH1, which encodes the collagen chaperone-like protein HSP47, that leads to a severe OI phenotype.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that a SERPINH1 mutation causes the disorder.

checks.claim: SERPINH1 encodes the collagen chaperone-like protein HSP47.
checks.evidence_quote: SERPINH1, which encodes the collagen chaperone-like protein HSP47

paragraphs.text: Christiansen et al. (2010) reported an individual with a severe osteogenesis imperfecta phenotype. Type I procollagen accumulated in the Golgi of fibroblasts from the affected individual.

checks.evidence_quote: in SERPINH1, which encodes the collagen chaperone-like protein HSP47, that leads to a severe OI phenotype
checks.explanation: The abstract describes a severe phenotype in the affected individual.

checks.claim: Type I procollagen accumulated in the Golgi of fibroblasts from the individual with OI10 reported by Christiansen et al. (2010).
checks.evidence_quote: Type I procollagen accumulates in the Golgi of fibroblasts from the affected individual

paragraphs.text: Duran et al. (2015) studied a patient with osteogenesis imperfecta who carried a SERPINH1 mutation.

checks.claim: Duran et al. (2015) studied a patient with osteogenesis imperfecta who carried a SERPINH1 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified a new OI mutation in SERPINH1 that results in destabilization and mislocalization of HSP47 and secondarily has similar effects on FKBP65.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a new OI mutation in SERPINH1, which implies an affected individual. It does not explicitly say a single patient was studied, and it gives no clinical details. Only the abstract was available.

paragraphs.text: Christiansen et al. (2010) found normal 3-hydroxylation of proline-986 in proalpha1(I) chains in their patient, placing HSP47 function downstream of the CRTAP/P3H1/CyPB prolyl 3-hydroxylation complex.

checks.evidence_quote: The normal 3-hydroxylation of the prolyl residue at position 986 of the triple helical domain of proalpha1(I) chains

checks.claim: Normal proline-986 3-hydroxylation in the SERPINH1-mutant patient places HSP47 function downstream of the CRTAP/P3H1/CyPB prolyl 3-hydroxylation complex.
checks.evidence_quote: places the role of HSP47 downstream from the CRTAP/P3H1/CyPB complex that is involved in prolyl 3-hydroxylation

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of OI10 in the patient reported by Christiansen et al. (2010) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance; the patient was homozygous for a SERPINH1 mutation.

paragraphs.text: In an individual with severe autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta, Christiansen et al. (2010) identified a homozygous missense mutation (c.233T-C, leu78-to-pro; L78P) in the SERPINH1 gene, which encodes the collagen chaperone HSP47. The L78P mutation led to proteasomal degradation of endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-resident HSP47; type I procollagen accumulated in the Golgi of patient fibroblasts, and a population of the secreted type I procollagen was protease sensitive.

checks.explanation: The abstract describes a severe recessive OI patient.

checks.explanation: The variant matches, and the title states homozygosity.

paragraphs.text: Duran et al. (2015) identified a new mutation in SERPINH1 in a patient with osteogenesis imperfecta. The mutation resulted in destabilization and mislocalization of HSP47 and secondarily had similar effects on FKBP65.

checks.evidence_quote: We have identified a new OI mutation in SERPINH1
checks.explanation: The new SERPINH1 OI mutation is stated. The abstract does not explicitly mention a patient or how many patients there were. Only the abstract was available.

paragraphs.text: On the basis of their findings in fibroblasts from a patient homozygous for the L78P mutation in SERPINH1, Christiansen et al. (2010) suggested that HSP47 monitors the integrity of the type I procollagen triple helix at the ER/cis-Golgi boundary and that, in its absence, ER-to-Golgi transit is increased and helical structure is compromised.

checks.explanation: The abstract reports fibroblast studies, and the title states homozygosity for the mutation.

(2015) found evidence that HSP47 and FKBP65 act cooperatively during posttranslational maturation of type I procollagen and fail to interact properly in cells with mutant HSP47, suggesting a common cellular pathway in osteogenesis imperfecta caused by HSP47 and FKBP65 deficiency.

paragraphs.text: In an individual with severe autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta (OI10), Christiansen et al. (2010) identified a homozygous c.233T-C transition in the SERPINH1 gene, resulting in a leu78-to-pro (L78P) substitution in HSP47. The mutation led to proteasomal degradation of ER-resident HSP47. Type I procollagen accumulated in the Golgi of the patient's fibroblasts, and part of the secreted type I procollagen was protease sensitive.
